# deepresearch-arms-lab

> deepresearch-arms-lab is a 14-arm ablation study on deep-research pipeline design that measures which prompt and pipeline mechanisms actually reduce citation fabrication on a weak base model, for engineers building autonomous research agents.

One question, answered with numbers instead of intuition: can a weak Chinese base model write a good research report *and* avoid fabricating citations? Fourteen prompt/pipeline designs ("arms") were built as runnable code, evaluated with one shared harness — Claude Opus 4.8 blind judging (median of 3) for quality, fact-v2 clause-level support rate for faithfulness — all on the same base model (MiMo 2.5 Pro), the same search backend and the same questions. The headline result is a **negative** one and is stated as such: at n=24 all three structural mechanisms score *below* the bare baseline on judged quality, and the earlier "dual-optimal winner" claim was retracted when the question set grew. Install with `pip install -r requirements.txt`; the results dashboard needs no server at all.

## Docs
- [Interactive results dashboard](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/dashboard.html): quality-vs-faithfulness scatter, arm rankings, experiment timeline; click any arm or topic for the original question, the full report and the scoring rationale
- [Full experiment log](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/EXPERIMENTS.html): every round in order, including the retracted conclusions and the contamination incident that became a finding
- [Method, experiments and staged conclusions](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/deepresearch-progress-report.html): the write-up of the problem framing and what each round established
- [Hybrid-v6 report](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/hybrid-v6-report.html): mechanism design, comparison results and where it fell short
- [F9.1 vs B3 report](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/f91-vs-b3-report.html): is evidence-bound writing worth it — the paired 10-question comparison
- [Survey of mainstream deep-research systems](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/research-dr-mainstream-20260720.html): how OpenAI, Gemini, Perplexity, STORM, GPT-Researcher and deer-flow handle citation, as of 2026-07-20
- [Evidence ledger for that survey](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/evidence-dr-mainstream.html): every statement with source URL, verbatim excerpt and a confidence label
- [Literature reading notes (training-free lens)](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/deepresearch-survey-notes.html): ten 2026 papers read in full, with cost and gain per approach
- [Technical survey report](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/docs-report-snapshot.html): the four families of non-training methods and the selection reasoning
- [Third-party notices](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.html): attribution for the 14 DeepResearch Bench questions used in the n=24 comparison

## Evidence
- [claims.json](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/claims.json): every number below with its metric, method, repro command and evidence link
- [Per-question evaluation data](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/qa_data.json): the raw question/report/score payload the dashboard renders
- F115 (three-stage pipeline) at n=24: judge **7.77** vs baseline **7.85** (−0.08), faithfulness **0.66** vs **0.42** (+0.24) — a real trade-off, not a free win
- F11 (source-side pre-citation) at n=24: judge **7.59** (−0.26), faithfulness **0.68** (+0.26) — the biggest faithfulness gain and the biggest quality cost
- F10.2 (post-hoc verification) at n=24: judge **7.59** (−0.26), faithfulness **0.54** (+0.12)
- The headline moved as the test set grew: F115's judge advantage over the baseline was **+0.66 at n=10, +0.12 at n=15, −0.08 at n=24**. Verified in [EXPERIMENTS.md](https://alloevil.github.io/deepresearch-arms-lab/EXPERIMENTS.html), where the superseded claims are left in place rather than edited out.
- Negative result kept: a key-claims registry maintained during writing (F9.1) gave **0.48 vs 0.48** faithfulness against a plain citation-protocol prompt (B3) at n=10, with roughly doubled latency
- Preliminary and labelled as such: GPT-Researcher on the same weak base model scored judge **5.75** / faithfulness **0.45** at **n=3**
